title: 2026-05-13 POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-Live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on planning the rollout/cutover from pilot to production. Agreed on a staged canary (5% -> 20% -> 100%), a dry-run, and required monitoring + alerting. Action items include sharing a detailed runbook, scheduling a dry-run with SRE, and updating the dashboard alerts. Customer emphasized SOC 2 controls, VPC peering validation, and rollback SLAs.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, gonna kick off the POC weekly. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Alex Martinez: Alex here.
[00:07] Priya Singh: Priya on product.
[00:09] Tom Reynolds: Tom, SRE.
[00:10] Maya Flores: Maya from security.
[00:12] Rita Kapoor: Rita from Redwood SE, hi.
[00:14] Liam Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: rollout plan, canary/A-B approach, monitoring and runbooks, cutover windows, and next steps.
[00:30] Priya: We did the pilot traffic split last week, performance looked good, but Tom has some concerns about tail latency when sequences go beyond 1k tokens.
[00:45] Tom: Yeah during the stress run we saw 95th jump to ~420ms, and occasional p99 spikes toward 1.2s, which is above our SLA. Not a dealbreaker but we need mitigation before ramp.
[01:02] Rita: Noted. Those spikes align with KV cache misses in our test config; in production with warm prefixes it should be lower. Also can enable continuous batching and small quantization tweak, but that trades off some quality.
[01:20] Alex: Quality matters, we can't have hallucination regressions. Priya is tracking acceptance thresholds.
[01:28] Priya: Correct. We want to keep >0.92 pass rate on our eval set. If tuning drops it we need to revert.
[01:35] Liam: Ok, let's move to canary. Proposal: 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor key metrics (latency p95, p99, error rate, correctness on eval set), then move to 20% for 24-48 hours, then full cutover. Any objections?
[01:52] Tom: 5% sounds fine but need a dry-run first (no customer traffic) to run through rollback and alerting. We want automation around rollback.
[02:02] Rita: We can run a dry-run in the staging cluster tomorrow. We'll also test canary routing policy in the Redwood console and the automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if errors spike.
[02:18] Maya: From security: need to validate VPC peering and KMS key access, plus audit log retention for SOC 2. Send us the SOC 2 artifact and KMS policy.
[02:29] Liam: Will do. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[02:33] Alex: On timing, we were thinking about a cutover window next Thursday 02:00-04:00 UTC. Any constraints?
[02:40] Tom: That window is okay but we need the dry-run 48 hours before and SE to be on-call for the first hour.
[02:47] Samir: We can provide an on-call rotation for the first two hours post-cutover.
[02:52] Priya: A/B testing question — can we route only a subset of users for a longer time to compare quality metrics?
[02:58] Rita: Yes, Redwood supports rule-based routing; A/B is doable. We recommend using canary first then a longer A/B for a select cohort if you need behavioral metrics.
[03:10] Alex: Also want to ensure traceability back to request IDs for debugging. Tom, can you confirm what spans you need?
[03:17] Tom: We need request ID in logs, and a sampled trace that includes the model version and shard id.
[03:23] Rita: We already emit a request_id header and model.version tag. Shard id sometimes gets munged in transcription here but it's in logs.
[03:31] Maya: About audit logs: retention of 1 year is required, and we need to demonstrate access controls.
[03:36] Liam: We'll include retention policy in the compliance docs and outline SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC.
[03:42] Priya: Rollback criteria? We need concrete thresholds.
[03:47] Tom: Suggest rollback if error rate >0.5% sustained for 5 minutes OR p99 >1.5s for 10 minutes OR eval pass rate drops more than 3 percentage points.
[03:58] Rita: Makes sense. We'll wire those as alerting rules in the dashboard and an automated policy to shift traffic back to previous model variant.
[04:07] Alex: Who will own the runbook? It should list steps, contacts, CLI commands to rollback, and postmortem template.
[04:15] Liam: Redwood will draft the runbook; BlueWave to review and sign-off. We'll include dry-run checklist.
[04:21] Priya: Also need a canary success checklist — metrics, QA sign-off, and security validations.
[04:27] Liam: Ok, timeline recap: dry-run on Tuesday (05/19) in staging, cutover Thursday 05/21 02:00-04:00 UTC, with 5% -> 20% -> full over the next 72 hours pending checks.
[04:40] Tom: I want the ability to pause the rollout and automatically revert to the dedicated reserved pool if needed. Is that supported?
[04:47] Rita: Yes, routing policies can failover to dedicated capacity or to a different model. We'll show the config in the console during the dry-run.
[04:55] Maya: Encryption at rest, KMS usage: confirm customer-managed keys are enabled for the private deployment.
[05:01] Liam: For your Dedicated setup we can use your KMS - we'll share integration guide.
[05:05] Priya: Any impact to cost we should plan for during the canary?
[05:09] Samir: There will be some overhead for duplicated traffic in A/B and for canary logging, but it's small relative to baseline. We'll provide an estimated cost delta after we size throughput.
[05:18] Alex: Ok good. Next steps?
[05:20] Liam: I'll summarize action items. Also we'll send the detailed runbook and SOC 2 pack.
[05:24] Priya: Please include the alert thresholds and dashboard links.
[05:27] Rita: We'll schedule the dry-run with Tom and Samir and share invites.
[05:30] Maya: Security will review KMS doc and get back with any constraints.
[05:33] Liam: Great, thanks everyone.
[05:36] Alex: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:38] Liam: End meeting.
